findings: Ward CAD's current public detail separately displays Interest Type RI, Decimal Interest and Category Code G1 and carries a research-information caveat; the public copy does not reproduce the sample owner's identity or decimal.

Pritchard & Abbott's current royalty-owner FAQ expands RI as royalty interest in its own examples, while its separate current page identifies Ward CAD as a client. The article explicitly does not treat those vendor pages as a Ward-issued code dictionary or an owner-specific title or payment rule.

Tarrant Appraisal District's 2025-2029 RFQ PDF page 19, in the 2024 mineral data-exchange appendix, separately identifies Owner Interest Type and Owner Decimal Interest of Ownership and expands RI as Royalty Interest. The complete reviewed PDF SHA-256 is 36be3c3bdd1874b0501e700be1c55b166610d0f70f96e74b9b67a3fce289e218. The article limits this legend and G1 description to Tarrant's contract rather than importing its fields into Ward.
The Texas RRC well-records source supports only the statement that private property-rights, lease and royalty-payment matters fall outside RRC authority; it is not cited for CAD semantics.

The conclusion that a displayed code and decimal do not alone prove a particular reader's title or payable share is a bounded inference from the distinct source roles, not a source quote or parcel-specific adjudication. No numeric result, deadline, valuation or royalty amount is asserted.
